Looking to join a world-class blockchain development team? Ava Labs makes it simple to deploy high-performance solutions for Web3, led by innovations on Avalanche. The company was founded by Cornell computer scientists, who partnered with Wall Street veterans and early Web3 leaders to execute a promising vision for redefining the way people build permissionless networks. Ava Labs is redefining the way people create value with Web3. Join us as we empower people to easily and freely digitize all the world’s assets on one open, programmable blockchain platform.

We are seeking a Senior Full-Stack Engineer to join the team building Fortary, our institutional digital asset custody platform. In this frontend-leaning role, you will deliver product capabilities end-to-end, from data modeling and API design on our TypeScript backend to the web experience institutions rely on to manage, approve, and stake digital assets across multiple blockchains. You will help shape a platform where security, correctness, and clarity are fundamental to the client experience.

Must be able to work US Eastern Time Zone hours or based in a location that allows consistent availability during U.S. Eastern Time business hours.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Deliver Features End-to-End: Lead features from data model and API design through to a refined, responsive user interface, including transaction and approval workflows, staking, portfolio and reporting views, and administrative tooling.

  • Shape the Web Experience: Build and evolve our React web application, partnering with Design to translate complex institutional workflows into interfaces that are clear, intuitive, and trustworthy.

  • Build Robust APIs: Design and implement backend services and integrations with custody infrastructure, blockchain data providers, and third-party platforms, keeping a well-defined, typed contract between frontend and backend.

  • Engineer for Humans and Agents: Keep our codebases clear, well-structured, and easy for both engineers and AI agents to navigate. Record architectural decisions in ADRs, and maintain the agent instructions and reusable skills that encode how we build, test, and ship.

  • Champion Security and Correctness: Treat authorization, approval policies, transaction transparency, and precise financial data handling as core product requirements, working closely with Security and Compliance to uphold SOC 2 controls and support regulatory readiness.

  • Drive Product Advancements: Assess client needs, recommend solutions, and collaborate with Product to incorporate client feedback, shape the roadmap, and recommend technical solutions to client needs.

  • Collaborate Across Teams: Work closely with Product, Design, and engineers across our signing, mobile, and infrastructure teams.

WHAT MAKES YOU A GOOD FIT

  • Frontend Depth, Backend Fluency: Deep expertise in modern frontend engineering, complemented by hands-on experience building and operating production backend systems.

  • Product and Design Sensibility: A strong eye for design and a user-centric approach, with the judgment to make sound UX decisions and carry ideas from early concepts to polished implementation.

  • Ownership: A self-directed mindset and full accountability for delivering high-quality, secure solutions.

  • AI-Native Engineering: You use AI coding agents as a core part of how you work, moving faster without lowering the bar, and you review AI-generated code with the same rigor and ownership as your own.

  • Adaptability: Comfort in a fast-moving environment where priorities evolve as our clients and goals grow.

  • Strong Communication: The ability to lead both deeply technical and high-level discussions, advocate clearly for the best approach, and remain open to feedback.

WHAT YOU WILL BRING

  • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, primarily frontend, with substantial production backend experience.

  • Expert-level TypeScript and strong React fundamentals.

  • Experience with the TanStack ecosystem (Query, Router, Form, Table), Tailwind CSS, and Zod or comparable libraries.

  • Experience building complex, data-heavy web applications, such as large tables, multi-step forms, and approval workflows, with attention to performance, accessibility, and consistency with a design system.

  • Production Node.js experience, including REST API design, PostgreSQL, and an ORM such as Drizzle.

  • A disciplined approach to testing across unit, integration, and end-to-end levels (e.g., Vitest, Playwright).

  • A security-first mindset, including authentication and authorization (JWT, RBAC), rigorous input validation, and building auditability and observability into the product.

NICE TO HAVES

  • Experience with Fastify, Redis, Temporal (or a similar workflow engine), and OpenTelemetry.

  • Experience with OpenAPI-driven development and generated API clients.

  • Background in the Web3, DeFi, or digital asset industry, particularly across multiple chains (EVM, Bitcoin, Solana).

  • Familiarity with custody and wallet UX, such as enterprise approval workflows, staking, and hardware wallet signing.

  • Experience with React Native and Expo.

  • Exposure to infrastructure and delivery tooling, including Docker, GitHub Actions, and Kubernetes.

WHY AVA LABS?

Ava Labs builds Avalanche, the blockchain platform institutions use to bring finance onchain. Since Avalanche launched in 2020, we have helped exchanges, banks, asset managers and fintechs move from experiments to live products, from tokenized funds and private credit to stablecoin payments and, now, the clearing and settlement ledger for the NYSE’s upcoming tokenized securities platform. Avalanche lets institutions run their own purpose-built networks with the performance, costs and participation controls they need, while staying connected to a broad ecosystem of DeFi protocols, liquidity and developers.

We are a team of experts in engineering, finance, economics, product and law, headquartered in New York City. You will work alongside people who have built at leading banks, exchanges and crypto companies, with the scope to shape how capital markets move onchain over the next decade. Ava Labs is backed by investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Polychain Capital and Initialized Capital.

Ava Labs is committed to diversity in the workplace and we’re proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not hire on the basis of race, color, religion, creed, gender, national origin, citizenship, age, disability, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy, parental status, sex, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, or any other basis protected by local, state or federal law. All employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, merit, and business need.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them.

A few things that define how we operate:

  • One team, one company, one objective. There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle.

  • If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it. We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack.

  • We go first, and we go fast. When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed.

  • We lead the way. We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job.

  • We stay calibrated. Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters.

You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure.

Our Teams

Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does.

Right now, we operate across five areas:

  • Compute — the foundation for running Ramp’s services and financial workflows: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and asynchronous execution and messaging systems, including Temporal. The team owns production runtime reliability, scaling, isolation, and safe rollouts.

  • Storage — the production data foundations that underpin Ramp: databases, caching, and object storage, with ownership of reliability, performance, capacity, recovery, and safe data movement.

  • Developer Infrastructure — the shared infrastructure that helps engineers ship and understand production: CI/CD systems, observability foundations for logs, metrics, and traces, and visibility into infrastructure usage and cost.

  • Compliance Platform — the infrastructure and operational capabilities for Ramp’s government environments and compliance needs: secure access, deployment paths, environment validation, and technical controls that let product teams deliver reliably within regulatory and compliance requirements.

  • Reliability Platform — the tools and operating model for understanding and improving customer-facing reliability and performance: SLA/SLO measurement and reporting, customer-health visibility, monitoring and paging, and incident response and follow-through. The team helps product teams remain accountable for the health of what they build.

What You'll Do

As a FinOps Specialist within Production Engineering, you’ll help Ramp make better decisions about infrastructure spend – from resource usage and cloud commitments to vendor contracts and new investments.

You’ll work closely with Production Engineering leadership, Developer Infrastructure, Finance, Procurement, and engineering teams across Ramp. You’ll bring financial depth, investigate opportunities independently, and partner with engineers to turn recommendations into measurable results.

This is a senior individual contributor role.

Day to day, you will:

  • Set direction for infrastructure cost management. Identify the highest-impact opportunities across Ramp, establish priorities with Production Engineering leadership and partner teams, and build a roadmap that balances immediate savings with lasting improvements.

  • Understand and explain our spend. Investigate costs across AWS, observability, and AI providers. Connect changes to usage, architecture, customer growth, and engineering decisions, and help teams distinguish expected investment from avoidable waste.

  • Embed with teams early. Partner with product and infrastructure teams during design and planning. Help them evaluate cost implications, model how systems will scale, and make informed tradeoffs before committing to an architecture or vendor.

  • Build forecasts we can defend. Work with engineers to understand upcoming launches, migrations, and capacity needs. Translate those plans into financial models that explain expected spend, key assumptions, and uncertainty.

  • Shape commitment and vendor strategy. Model cloud discounts, commitment levels, payment structures, and renewal scenarios. Partner with Finance, Procurement, and infrastructure leaders to develop negotiation strategies and carry them through vendor discussions.

  • Drive optimization across the company. Proactively identify opportunities that span teams, propose a path forward, align engineering owners and technical program managers, and stay involved through implementation and verified savings.

  • Make cost visible and actionable. Partner with DevInfra to build attribution, dashboards, anomaly detection, and self-service tools that let teams understand and manage their costs. Establish reusable approaches that make cost awareness part of how Ramp builds, and work toward clearer service and product unit economics.

  • Evaluate new infrastructure investments. Build models for decisions such as buying versus renting capacity, changing providers, or adopting new infrastructure. Make the financial implications and technical assumptions clear.

  • Use AI to investigate and build. Use AI tools and coding agents to analyze data, create dashboards and automations, navigate infrastructure code, and develop proposed changes with engineering partners. Help improve the tools and workflows that make cost management repeatable.

What We Look For

We don’t hire for a checklist. We hire for the judgment and ownership that make someone effective in this role.

The mindset we’re looking for:

  • You follow the question through. When a bill changes, you want to understand what happened, whether it makes sense, and what to do about it.

  • You have high agency. You identify opportunities without waiting for an assignment, investigate independently, and bring a recommendation. When progress depends on other teams, you find the right partners and drive the work forward.

  • You think in systems and tradeoffs. You connect technical decisions to financial outcomes and weigh savings against reliability, performance, engineering time, and flexibility.

  • You look for the underlying cause. When you uncover unexpected spend or an inefficient process, you investigate what allowed it to happen and improve the tooling, decisions, or practices that will prevent it from recurring.

  • You connect efficiency to customer outcomes. You partner closely with engineering teams to understand their goals and make cost tradeoffs that help Ramp serve customers reliably and scale sustainably. You pursue savings with a clear understanding of their impact on performance, reliability, and the team’s ability to deliver.

  • You make complex things understandable. You can discuss financial models with Finance and infrastructure choices with engineers, and help both make decisions together.

  • You own the outcome. You set priorities, build alignment, and follow through to implementation and measured results. You turn what you learn into tools and practices that help teams make better decisions themselves.

Experience profile:

  • Experience improving infrastructure economics in a growing technology organization, with examples of decisions you influenced and measurable results you helped deliver.

  • Strong financial modeling and forecasting skills. You can translate engineering roadmaps, customer growth, migrations, and new infrastructure investments into future spend scenarios. You make assumptions and uncertainty explicit, explain variances, and update forecasts as plans evolve.

  • Experience planning large infrastructure contracts and commitments. You can model usage over multi-year terms, compare pricing and payment structures, and balance savings against overcommitment risk and flexibility. You’ve helped shape commitment levels, renewal timing, and negotiation strategy with Finance, Procurement, and engineering leaders.

  • Working knowledge of cloud billing and pricing, including cost allocation, commitment discounts, payment structures, and the relationship between usage and cost. AWS experience is especially relevant.

  • Strong technical fluency. You can reason about compute, storage, networking, and managed services, and navigate Terraform or similar infrastructure-as-code tools to understand how systems are configured. You can investigate technical questions independently, connect infrastructure choices to cost, and work with engineers on concrete changes.

  • Experience with cost attribution and analysis. You can connect infrastructure spend to teams, services, products, and usage drivers, including shared resources. You work directly with cost and usage data, reconcile conflicting sources, and develop practical allocation methods with clear assumptions.

  • A record of initiating and driving work across teams, from identifying an opportunity and building the case to coordinating implementation and validating the result.

  • Practical experience using AI tools and coding agents to analyze data, build dashboards or automations, and investigate technical questions. You can evaluate their output and recognize when deeper engineering review is needed.

Relevant backgrounds include FinOps, infrastructure finance, strategic sourcing, analytics, data, and infrastructure engineering. A software engineering background is welcome, but not required.

Bonus (not required):

  • Deep experience with AWS Cost and Usage Reports, Savings Plans, or Reserved Instances.

  • Cost management for Datadog, other observability platforms, or AI providers.

  • Product unit economics or infrastructure accounting classifications.

  • Financial analysis of large migrations, dedicated compute, or data center investments.

  • Experience in fintech, payments, or regulated industries, with an understanding of how compliance, security, and data residency requirements shape infrastructure choices and costs.

Who We Are

Solana is the leading high-performance network powering internet capital markets, payments, and crypto applications, built to become the capital market for every asset on earth. Anza is the core engineering team behind it. Founded by the engineers who built the original Solana validator client at Solana Labs, we develop Agave, the network’s primary and most widely run validator client, and ship the software that pushes the boundaries of blockchain performance and scale.

We advance the frontier of Solana’s core protocol. Most recently, Anza built and shipped Alpenglow, the biggest upgrade in Solana’s history, replacing the network’s original consensus protocol and bringing deterministic finality in about 150ms to mainnet-beta. And we’re just getting started, with work underway on faster block propagation, quicker leader handoffs, and the infrastructure that will carry Solana’s next phase of growth.

The Role

As a Software Engineer specializing in storage, you will play a critical role in fortifying Anza’s Agave client and the broader Solana network. The AccountsDB team owns the custom storage engine at the heart of every Solana validator. Every account on Solana, from balances to program state to token holdings, lives in AccountsDB, and every transaction the network processes reads from and writes to it.

Your work will directly contribute to the performance and reliability of our blockchain infrastructure, ensuring account state is stored, indexed, and served efficiently as the network grows. 

Responsibilities

  • Develop and Optimize the Storage Engine: Design, implement, and optimize AccountsDB’s core storage paths, including account file layout, the account index, and the read and write caching layers, to improve throughput and latency across the validator.
  • Reduce Resource Footprint: Lower memory and disk requirements as account state continues to grow, to keep validator hardware requirements in check.
  • Background Services: Improve the flushing, cleaning, shrinking, and purging processes to reduce write amplification and keep resource usage predictable under sustained load.
  • Snapshots and Startup: Optimize snapshot generation, loading, and index generation to shorten validator startup and catch-up times.
  • Correctness and Integrity: Ensure account state remains correct across forks, rooting, and crash recovery, where bugs can have network-wide consequences.
  • Testing and Validation: Create and execute comprehensive tests to validate the reliability and efficiency of the storage engine, including stress tests, fault injection, and performance benchmarking.
  • Collaboration: Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including runtime, block production, and core protocol engineers, as well as other Solana client teams, to ensure seamless integration of storage components across the validator.
  • Documentation and Code Review: Maintain thorough documentation of AccountsDB design and behavior and conduct peer code reviews to uphold high standards of code quality and consistency.

What You'll Bring

  • Systems Engineering Background: Bachelor’s degree in CS, Engineering, or relevant practical experience, alongside 3+ years architecting data stores, file systems, databases, or high-throughput storage systems.
  • Systems Languages & Storage Architecture: Mastery of Rust, C, or C++. Comprehensive grasp of low-level storage mechanics, including memory-mapped files, page caching, index structures, on-disk formats, and garbage collection mechanisms.
  • I/O Subsystems: Advanced knowledge of kernel-level and hardware I/O pipelines, NVMe constraints, buffered versus direct I/O, and modern async interfaces like io_uring.
  • Kernel & Memory Management: Strong understanding of custom memory allocators and Linux kernel scheduling, page management, and I/O handling under intense throughput.
  • Concurrent Programming: Proven experience building concurrent systems, featuring deep knowledge of lock overhead, lock-free structures, and hardware memory models.
  • Profiling and Optimization: Track record of profiling and tuning low-level code with an emphasis on hardware mechanics, memory bus saturation, and CPU cache efficiency.
  • Systemic Problem Solving: Ability to debug intricate software architectures, isolate performance bottlenecks, and execute robust engineering solutions.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Exceptional communication skills and a team-first mindset for working alongside technical peers in an open environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with LSM trees, B-trees, or hash-based storage engines such as RocksDB, LevelDB, or WiredTiger.
  • Background in versioned or multi-version data stores, snapshotting systems, or blockchain state storage.
  • Familiarity with Linux, systems automation tools, and systems architecture.
  • Active participation in Bitcoin/Ethereum/Blockchain projects or the open-source community is highly desirable.

Why Join Anza?

We offer a dynamic, fast-paced environment where innovation and problem-solving are at the heart of everything we do. Here, your work will have a direct impact on the security and scalability of blockchain technology, contributing to the foundation of decentralized applications worldwide.

We're excited to welcome individuals who share our passion for pushing the boundaries of blockchain technology. If you're ready to take on the challenge and contribute to the next generation of blockchain infrastructure, we'd love to hear from you.

Reports to:

Director, Engineering, CoinDesk

At CoinDesk, we do more than report on the future of money. We actively help shape it. As the global leader in crypto news, indices, and events, we provide the transparency and context the world needs to understand the digital asset revolution. Our team is dedicated to a shared mission: informing, educating, and connecting the global community.

Our impact is amplified by our position within the Bullish Group. Bullish is a regulated, institutional-grade exchange known for technological prowess. Operating as a subsidiary, CoinDesk is backed by a partner that shares our belief in the transformative power of digital assets.

We value engineers who treat development as a craft. You will own outcomes from concept to deployment. We expect you to navigate the unknown and bring structure to ambiguity. Who we are:

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom. OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). About the opportunity:

We are looking for an experienced, commercially aware, and regulatory-savvy compliance professional to join us as Head of Compliance and Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO).
The role will be instrumental in building the compliance programme from the ground up, and embedding a culture of compliance across the organisation.
Broader team management responsibilities will be added in due course for regulatory strategy, operational execution, and governance.

Key Responsibilities:

Regulatory Engagement

  • Serve as the primary point of contact with relevant regulatory bodies.
  • Ensure the organisation meets all applicable governance requirements, including fit and proper obligations for Approved and Designated Persons.
  • Monitor and interpret regulatory developments relevant to virtual assets, and advise senior management and the Board accordingly.

Compliance Programme Development & Management

  • Design, implement, and maintain a comprehensive compliance framework aligned with local requirements, FATF recommendations, and international best practice for virtual asset service providers (VASPs).
  • Develop, review, and update all internal policies and procedures covering AML/CFT, KYC, customer due diligence (CDD), enhanced due diligence (EDD), transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, data protection, cybersecurity compliance, and safeguarding of client assets.
  • Establish and oversee the compliance monitoring programme, including periodic testing, gap analysis, and reporting to senior management and the Board.
  • Prepare and present regular compliance reports to the Board and relevant committees, including on regulatory changes, compliance breaches, and remediation progress.
  • Ensure compliance considerations are integrated into new product design and operations from the inception phase by driving solutions that balance commercial outcomes and innovation, while maintaining a robust compliance posture using a clear risk-based approach.
  • Review technical documentation, user journeys, and product flows to ensure compliance risks are addressed; provide clear, actionable and solution-focused advice during the product lifecycle.
  • Build and scale compliance policies governing advertising, social media campaigns, influencer partnerships, and product launches.
  • Partner with Legal, Product, and Marketing teams to operationalize a timely review process for client-facing assets and go-to-market materials.

AML/CFT & MLRO Duties

  • Act as the designated MLRO, with full statutory responsibility for overseeing the organisation's AML/CFT framework.
  • Receive, review, and assess all internal Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) from staff, and make informed decisions on whether to file external disclosures with competent local authorities.
  • Oversee and continuously improve the transaction monitoring programme, with support from global compliance and product functions.
  • Ensure robust sanctions screening against all applicable lists, including OFAC, UK OFSI, UN, EU, and applicable local sanctions designations.
  • Oversee customer risk scoring, risk-based KYC/CDD processes, and enhanced due diligence for high-risk customers, politically exposed persons (PEPs), and customers from high-risk jurisdictions.

Governance & Culture

  • Act as a key member of the senior leadership team, providing compliance input on new products, services, partnerships, and business initiatives.
  • Champion a strong compliance culture across the organisation through training, communications, and leadership by example.
  • Design and deliver AML/CFT and compliance training programmes for all staff, ensuring completion records are maintained.
  • Ensure that the organisation's compliance obligations are adequately resourced, and advise the Board on staffing, systems, and budget requirements.
  • Establish and maintain a compliance manual, risk register and oversee the escalation and resolution of compliance incidents and breaches.

Reporting & Recordkeeping

  • Prepare and submit all required regulatory reports and notifications to relevant authorities within stipulated deadlines.
  • Ensure that all compliance records, SAR documentation, KYC files, and transaction monitoring records are maintained in accordance with applicable retention requirements.
  • Support and facilitate any inspections, supervisory visits, or regulatory examinations.

What We Look For in You

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Law, Finance, Business, or a related field. A postgraduate qualification is advantageous.
  • Professional certification in compliance or AML is strongly preferred (e.g. CAMS, ICA Certificate/Diploma in AML or Compliance, CFE, or equivalent).

Experience

  • Minimum of 8 years of experience in compliance, AML, or financial crime prevention, with at least 3 years in a senior or leadership compliance role.
  • Demonstrated in-house experience working within virtual asset service providers (VASPs), cryptocurrency exchanges, fintech firms, or regulated financial institutions.
  • Prior experience as an MLRO or Deputy MLRO is highly desirable.
  • Experience engaging directly with financial regulators and the financial intelligence unit
  • Hands-on experience building compliance programmes from the ground up in a start-up or scaling environment is a significant advantage.
  • Familiarity with the regional regulatory framework and requirements is strongly preferred.

Knowledge & Skills

  • Deep understanding of FATF Recommendations and their application to virtual asset service providers, including the Travel Rule (FATF Recommendation 16)
  • Strong knowledge of crypto-specific AML typologies.
  • Proficiency with blockchain analytics and transaction monitoring tools (e.g. Chainalysis, Elliptic, TRM Labs, or equivalent).
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and French.
  • Strong analytical and investigative skills, with the ability to identify and articulate complex risk scenarios clearly.
  • Demonstrated ability to engage constructively with regulators, external auditors, and law enforcement.
  • High degree of personal integrity and sound professional judgment.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in cryptocurrency or blockchain compliance programs.
  • Experience working in a multi-national financial institution setting.
  • Familiarity with compliance technology and analytics tools.
  • Prior exposure to multi-jurisdictional compliance oversight.
  • In-depth knowledge of crypto products, including spot trading, derivatives, staking, lending/borrowing, DeFi, and stablecoins.

descriptions.job-1wk1560:
Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

The Deployment Strategist, CTI role gets enterprise cyber threat intelligence (CTI) teams from a signed contract to repeatable intelligence outcomes on TRM's Intel platform. As the first Deployment Strategist dedicated to private sector CTI in North America, you will own each customer end to end, from onboarding through adoption, renewal, and expansion. What makes this role unique at TRM is the chance to define the function from scratch: you set the deployment playbook, the success metrics, and the standard the next hire inherits.

The impact you will have:

  • Get customers to real intelligence outcomes fast. Ship a working v1 deployment and onboarding playbook within your first 30 days, using Claude to turn customer call recordings and account notes into tailored onboarding plans.

  • Turn early wins into habit. Use Claude and TRM's Intel platform to move analysts from one-off searches to recurring workflows, such as threat landscape and sector targeting, vulnerability prioritization, credential and infostealer exposure, ransomware readiness, and malware and IOC investigation.

  • Free your time for judgment work. Build production AI workflows that pull from Salesforce, Gong, and product usage telemetry to auto-generate account health summaries and QBR drafts.

  • Catch risk before renewal. Define adoption benchmarks across your portfolio (hands-on usage, workflow adoption, consumption, and account-specific success metrics) and use AI-generated health signals to flag at-risk accounts well before renewal decisions.

  • Prove value with executives. Run business reviews with CISOs, CTI directors, and security leaders, using AI-drafted summaries that tie product usage to outcomes they report on, such as faster investigations, reduced exposure, and analyst time saved.

  • Grow every account. Co-own renewal and expansion with the Account Director, carry NRR and GRR targets alongside Sales, and use AI to find the next workflow, team, or use case worth expanding into.

  • Shape the product. Use AI to cluster adoption blockers, feature gaps, data coverage needs, and new use cases into prioritized input for Product, and build the deployment tooling the next hire will inherit.

What we’re looking for:

  • 5+ years in deployment strategy, onboarding, solutions engineering, customer success, or other post-sale roles, with proven ownership of NRR, GRR, and expansion metrics, and a record of using AI to scale that work.

  • Background in cyber threat intelligence, security operations, threat hunting, incident response, or a CTI vendor or platform environment (consulting, MSSP, and enterprise security teams all count).

  • Credibility with CTI practitioners: you understand how a corporate CTI team works (intelligence requirements, finished intelligence, handoffs to SOC and hunt teams), you're fluent in threat actors, MITRE ATT&CK, vulnerability and exploitation intelligence, ransomware, and stealer logs, and you use AI to sharpen that intelligence work and earn an analyst's trust in the first meeting.

  • Zero-to-one experience: you've built a deployment, onboarding, or customer success function or playbook from scratch, used AI to speed it up, and can point to the outcomes it produced.

  • Production AI fluency: you've built real, repeatable AI workflows (not just experiments) that synthesize data from multiple sources, and you can explain the data logic and where human judgment stays in the loop.

  • Executive presence: you can run a QBR with a CISO at a global bank or insurer and guide the room through substance, arriving prepared with AI-assisted briefs.

  • Experience supporting enterprise customers across North American time zones, including regulated industries such as financial services, insurance, telecom, and critical infrastructure, plus a bias to ship v1 before you have all the answers, with AI helping you move faster.

  • Nice to have: time at a threat intelligence vendor, an ISAC or ISAO, or a corporate intelligence team; familiarity with third-party and supply chain risk or cyber insurance workflows; certifications such as GCTI or GCIH.

About the Team:

  • This team focuses on TRM's Intel platform, supporting CTI and security teams at enterprises facing sophisticated cyber threats.

  • You'd be the first Deployment Strategist dedicated to private sector CTI in North America, with high ownership, direct access to leadership, and real influence on how TRM deploys and retains customers in this segment. The work stretches you: you set the agenda in a function that doesn't exist yet.

  • The broader customer team works distributed, not distant: async-first communication in Slack, strong documentation, and intentional synchronous time for key decisions.

  • You'll work directly with the Head of Customer Success and the CRO, with close day-to-day collaboration with North America Sales and Product, built on trust and direct feedback.

Team Operating Rhythms:

  • Distributed, not distant: we hold weekly customer syncs and biweekly health syncs, join POD calls, and regularly engage customers as trusted advisors.

  • Working hours and customer coverage align primarily with North American time zones, with flexibility to collaborate across regions when needed.

  • The team moves fast and iterates: v1 ships before it's perfect, and feedback is direct and specific.

  • Communication is async-first in Slack, with synchronous time reserved for customer work and key decisions.

Required online and collaboration hours:

  • Schedule: Primarily North American business hours, with occasional collaboration with customers outside US time zones if EMEA or APAC customers close earlier than expected.

On-Call Responsibilities:

  • Schedule: No formal on-call rotation. As the primary lead for your customers, you see mission-critical issues through to resolution, including urgent customer needs outside standard hours when they arise.

  • Frequency: Not applicable (no rotation).

Travel Requirements:

  • Schedule: Minimal. Most onboarding and enablement is virtual, with occasional travel to customers.

  • Frequency: About 10% of your time.

Onsite Requirements:

  • Schedule: No regular onsite requirement. Occasional customer visits are covered under travel.

  • Frequency: Occasional, included in the 10% travel estimate.

Learn about TRM Speed in this position:

  • A working v1 deployment playbook within 30 days: built from your first 2 to 3 accounts, with measurable adoption benchmarks, and already used by the account team to set customer expectations.

  • A draft success metrics framework at 50% complete within 6 weeks, shared with the account team and key customers to validate direction before further investment.

  • The highest-impact expansion play scoped within 60 days: worked backward from renewal and expansion targets, with a concrete recommendation to leadership on which workflow or use case to prioritize and why, grounded in account data.

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

  • Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

  • Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly

  • Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

  • Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

  • Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

  • Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore.

Privacy Policy and Additional Information

By submitting your application, you agree to allow TRM Labs to process your personal information in accordance with our Privacy Policy.

We collect the information you provide (such as your resume, work history, and contact details) solely for the purpose of evaluating your candidacy for current and future roles at TRM.

Because our hiring cycles for certain positions may span 24 to 36 months, we retain your personal information for up to 36 months from the date of your application. After that period, your data is deleted unless a different retention period is required or permitted by law.

If you are located in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or another jurisdiction with applicable data protection laws, you have the right to access, correct, or request deletion of your personal data at any time before that period ends. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at privacy@trmlabs.com.

To notify TRM Labs that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance.

The use of AI tools of any kind (including but not limited to notetakers, interview assistants, and real-time coaching tools such as Otter.ai, Fireflies, Fathom, Cluey, or similar) during TRM interviews is not permitted without prior approval from TRM. TRM uses its own internal tools for note-taking to ensure a consistent and confidential experience for all candidates.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this form.

Recruitment agencies

TRM Labs does not accept unsolicited agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to TRM employees. TRM Labs is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes and will not pay fees to any third-party agency or company without a signed agreement.

About Coinflow

Coinflow is the next-generation payment service provider revolutionizing global financial infrastructure with stablecoins, AI-driven fraud prevention, and instant settlement. Coinflow enables businesses to grow faster with instant settlement, fraud & chargeback indemnity, global pay-ins, multi-currency FX, and unified payouts. Founded in 2023, the company serves marketplaces, fintechs, remittance providers, gaming platforms, and ecommerce merchants worldwide.

Since our seed round in 2024, we’ve achieved 23x revenue growth and scaled to multi-billion-dollar annual transaction volume. In response to this growth, Coinflow announced a $25M Series A in October 2025—led by Pantera Capital, CMT Digital, Coinbase Ventures, Jump Crypto, and Reciprocal Ventures—accelerating our mission to power the world’s fastest-moving businesses with innovative, reliable global payments.

Coinflow is proudly headquartered in Chicago, IL. Learn more at coinflow.cash.

About The Role

We're hiring an MLOps Engineer to own the platform that takes our fraud, risk, and payments models from notebook to production. You'll build the pipelines, serving infrastructure, and monitoring that let us score every transaction in real time, retrain safely.

Our models sit in the authorization path of real money, so latency, reliability, and explainability matter as much as accuracy. You'll be hands-on with AI-native tooling: we use AI as a force multiplier for building pipelines, writing evals, and automating the boring parts of model operations. If you want to be one of the first ML infrastructure engineers building this way at a fast-growing PSP, you'll fit in well here.

What You'll Own

Real-Time Model Serving: Build and operate the inference layer that scores transactions in the authorization path. Hit tight latency budgets, design safe fallbacks when a model or feature is unavailable, and make sure a model outage never becomes a payments outage.

ML Pipelines & Feature Store: Own training, validation, and deployment pipelines end to end. Build reproducible feature pipelines from our transaction, device, and chargeback data, with point-in-time correctness so offline training matches online scoring.

Model Deployment & Rollout: Make shipping a model boring. Versioning, registries, shadow mode, champion/challenger, canary rollouts, and one-click rollback. Every change is gated by evals, not vibes.

Monitoring & Drift Detection: Instrument models the way we instrument services. Track latency, score distributions, feature drift, approval rates, and fraud and chargeback outcomes, wired into our observability stack with alerts that fire on real problems.

Third-Party Model Integration: Integrate and evaluate external fraud and risk vendors alongside our own models. Run parallel and shadow testing, compare performance on our data, and give the team a clear answer on what to trust.

Merchant-Facing Risk Tooling: Power the data and scoring behind our merchant-facing risk products, so merchants can see risky customers and set their own blocking rules on top of our signals.

What We're Looking For

  • 4+ years in MLOps, ML infrastructure, or ML platform engineering, ideally at a fintech, payments company, or other regulated environment

  • You've run models in production with real latency and uptime requirements, not just trained them. Experience with real-time inference in a transaction or decisioning path is a big plus

  • Strong Python and solid production engineering habits. Comfortable reading and writing TypeScript/Node, since that's where most of our services live

  • Hands-on experience with ML pipeline and serving tooling (MLflow, Kubeflow, SageMaker, Vertex, BentoML, Feast, or similar) and the judgment to know when not to use them

  • Solid infrastructure skills: containers, Kubernetes, CI/CD, and at least one major cloud provider

  • Data engineering chops: you can build reliable feature pipelines over operational, warehouse, and streaming data, and you understand training/serving skew

  • Experience monitoring models in production: drift, calibration, and tying model metrics back to business outcomes like fraud loss and approval rates

  • Familiarity with fraud, risk, or credit modeling, and with explaining model behavior to non-ML stakeholders like banks and auditors

  • Comfort working with AI-native tooling (Claude Code or similar) as a daily driver, or genuine excitement to start

  • A bias toward shipping. We'd rather have a working v1 of a model pipeline today than a perfect platform next quarter

The base salary range for this role is $120,000 - $180,000 USD + equity. The actual base salary offered depends on a variety of factors, including but not limited to experience, education, skills, qualifications, and business needs.

Join the team rewriting how money moves worldwide—and become a driving force in the $194 trillion cross-border payments market.
